objective_checks.detail: changing docs/guide.md routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing src/index.js routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing package-lock.json routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing README.md, LICENSE routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
required check(s) always fire and gate internally (.github/workflows/tests.yml)
event-only workflows carry no path filters (.github/workflows/nightly-sweep.yml, .github/workflows/triage.yml)

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: Every push/pull_request workflow got a deliberate decision, the schedule/issue workflows were correctly identified as filter-exempt, and the required `unit-tests` check was given exactly the working shape — one workflow, no workflow-level paths, a computed `run` output gating the real steps via `if:` with a success-reporting skip — rather than a companion skip workflow or a trigger-level filter.

dimensions.name: Salience
dimensions.rationale: Each workflow's paths/gate closely match what its own steps consume (deploy: src, package manifests, deploy.sh, itself; docs: docs/, mkdocs.yml, itself; tests: src/test/manifests/workflow), reflecting per-workflow reasoning rather than a shared catch-all, though the tests gate omits any test config the suite might read.

dimensions.name: Restraint
dimensions.rationale: It left nightly-sweep.yml and triage.yml untouched, did not touch the branch-protection ruleset, and edited only the three workflow files the audit implicated.
